newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat seeding progresses slowly.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat seeding progresses slowly.

text.p: Seeding of Kansas wheat fields progressed at a slow pace during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
Six percent of the state's wheat acreage was seeded, ahead of five percent last year but lagging the 12-percent average.

Harvest of fall crops picked up speed as crops continued to develop ahead of average. Corn condition was rated 82 percent good to excellent, 14 percent fair and four poor to very poor. Sixty percent of the corn was mature, versus 13 percent last year and the average of 44 percent.

Sorghum condition was rated 87 percent good to excellent, 12 percent fair and one percent poor. The crop was 25 percent mature, ahead of four percent last year and the average of 16 percent. Serious infestations of corn earworms were reported in sorghum fields in central and southern Kansas.
Soybeans were rated 82 percent good to excellent, 17 fair and one percent poor.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent very short, 24 percent short, 72 percent adequate and three percent surplus.
Pasture condition rated 75 percent good to excellent, 20 percent fair and five percent poor.
